AGNES.acting: She tends to the hawk until the unfamiliar man addresses her, remaining alert to his presence.
AGNES.head: HEAD-NONE

WILL.acting: He approaches with courteous uncertainty, drawn to Agnes but unsure how to begin.
WILL.head: HEAD-NONE

beats.acting: She turns her attention from the hawk to acknowledge him with guarded courtesy.
He returns the greeting carefully, trying to appear more composed than he feels.
Her greeting becomes a direct inquiry as she studies what has brought him to Hewlands.
The question makes him answer promptly but with visible social unease.
Hearing that she has already heard of him catches him off guard.
Her question about the garden makes him briefly avoid her eyes while searching for an acceptable answer.
She lightly teases his hesitation, making clear that she expects a straightforward answer.
He searches for an explanation, looking away momentarily as he gathers his thoughts.
The unfinished explanation exposes his embarrassment and renewed discomfort.
Mention of the bird gives him a safer subject and shifts his attention toward it.
His reference to the bird settles her attention on the hawk as the subject she would rather discuss.
She corrects him crisply, asserting the hawk's identity without abandoning her guarded composure.
The correction reveals his unfamiliarity and leaves him momentarily unsure how to respond.
